intro: If you're planning to use Krabi Town as a base for island trips and want a clean, affordable place you can walk everywhere from — Lada Krabi Residence is a name that comes up often among the budget stays in the Pak Nam area · It's a small 2-star place on Maharaj Road, open since 2012, with just 27 rooms, most of them with a small balcony plus air-con, TV, fridge and an en-suite bathroom · The thing guests agree on is the location: it's a few-minute walk to the Krabi Walking Street night market, close to Chao Fah Pier and the transport terminals, with friendly staff who help arrange island tours · Scored 8.1 from 43 reviews on Trip.com and 3.9 out of 5 on TripAdvisor (#4 of 29 stays in Pak Nam) · from about THB 900/night

body.html: Lada Krabi Residence at a glance — who it's for — If we boil it down to the shortest version, Lada Krabi Residence is a stay for people who see Krabi as a "starting point," not a "destination" · It's not a beachfront resort where you wake up and walk straight into the sea, and it's not a luxury hotel with a rooftop pool or a full spa · It's a small, budget 2-star place in central Krabi Town, in the Pak Nam area — a neighborhood where locals actually live, with markets, restaurants at Krabi prices, the pier, and the transport terminals all in one place · It's been open since 2012 with just 27 rooms, run like a family-managed stay rather than a big hotel chain · Real reviews on both Trip.com and TripAdvisor agree that the people who fit here are budget travelers, couples who'd rather be out exploring than lounging in the room, small families after a light rate, and anyone using Krabi as a base to take a boat to Poda Island, Chicken Island, the Separated Sea, or catch a ride on to Ao Nang and Koh Lanta · The ones who may be disappointed are people expecting a resort vibe, sea views, or full facilities, because this place sells simplicity, cleanliness and location, not luxury · Put another way, if you're coming to Krabi to go hard, using the room just to sleep and shower, then putting the money you save toward boat tours and seafood, Lada Krabi Residence does that job well at a price that's hard to find in this area

Location and getting around — This is unquestionably Lada Krabi Residence's number-one selling point · The stay sits on Maharaj Road, Soi 90/71-72, in the Pak Nam area, which is the genuine center of Krabi Town · What reviews mention most is that it's a few-minute walk to the Krabi Walking Street night market, open every Friday–Saturday–Sunday — a night market that gathers local food, snacks and souvenirs in one spot · You can also easily walk to the fresh market and local restaurants, which makes the cost per meal noticeably cheaper than over on the Ao Nang beach side · Getting out on a trip is convenient too, because Chao Fah Pier, where boats leave for Poda Island, Chicken Island, the Separated Sea and Railay, is a short walk away · The minivan and songthaew stop for Ao Nang is also nearby, about 20–25 minutes to Ao Nang beach · Krabi Airport (KBV) is about 13–14 km away, or roughly a 20 min drive · One thing to say honestly is that Krabi Town "isn't on the sea" — if the picture in your head is waking up to a white-sand beach, this isn't it; you'll need to take a car or boat out · But for people who understand that the town is the transport hub, this location saves a lot of both time and travel cost when you're heading out on trips several days in a row

"We chose to stay in town because we were heading out to the islands every day — turned out to be great value. The pier is a short walk away, in the evening we'd walk over to eat at the Walking Street market, the room was clean, and staff handled all the tour bookings for us. About half the price of staying in Ao Nang."

Room types and decor — Lada Krabi Residence has 27 rooms in all, split into a handful of types to choose from by group size and budget · Starting with the Superior Double Room, the entry-level room with one double bed, good for a solo traveler or a couple keeping costs down · Stepping up to the Deluxe Double Room with Balcony, which adds a double bed plus a small balcony you can sit out on for some air · There's the Deluxe Twin Room with Balcony at around 25 sqm, with two single beds plus a balcony, suited to friends or anyone who wants separate beds · And the largest is the Deluxe Quadruple Room, set up with two big beds and sleeping up to 4, good for a family or group of friends splitting the room cost · The decor is a simple style in light tones, with tiled floors that are easy to keep clean — nothing fancy, but plenty of reviews stress the same thing: the rooms are clean, the beds comfortable, and bigger than expected at this price · Every room has air-con, a flat-screen TV with cable, a fridge, a safe, a phone, and an en-suite bathroom with a shower and basic toiletries · One thing many people like is the private balcony on the Deluxe rooms, where you can sit with a morning coffee or hang up laundry after coming back from the sea · To be honest, some of the rooms are starting to show their age given the opening year (2012), and the paintwork and some of the furniture may look a bit worn in places — but cleanliness is what gets praised consistently, which matters more than newness for a budget stay · Anyone who wants a quiet room should ask for one away from the road or further inside when booking

Facilities and extra services — Set your expectations right from the start: Lada Krabi Residence is a small budget stay, with no swimming pool and no gym or rooftop bar like a big hotel · But the things you actually need are all here · There's a 24-hour front desk, which matters a lot for anyone arriving late or heading out by boat at dawn · There's free Wi-Fi (some reviews say the signal is strongest in the lobby, and may be weaker in some rooms — anyone needing to work online should plan for that) · There's a small massage and spa service to unwind after a full day of sightseeing · A point many people single out for praise is the staff who help arrange island tours, book transfers and recommend local restaurants, so first-timers in Krabi don't have to spend time digging up information themselves · Tour prices booked through the stay are usually about the same as booking outside, but more convenient and reassuring · There's also luggage storage, which is very useful for people who've checked out but still have an afternoon trip before catching a car or flight home · Overall the facilities here are "right for the price" — no luxury frills, but covering what hands-on travelers actually use

Breakfast and restaurants nearby — Lada Krabi Residence includes breakfast in the room rate, served on the ground floor of the building · It's a set with menu choices, with both Thai and American-style options such as eggs, bread, and tea or coffee · Most reviews say breakfast is "decent and fresh," and some praise it for having vegetarian options too, which is rare for a stay at this price · But there are some honest notes that the menu variety isn't huge — it's not a big buffet — and the seating area sometimes has no air-con, so it can get warm later in the morning · What helps cover this limitation is the location, because the area around the stay is full of local restaurants at Krabi prices, from morning curry-rice shops and traditional coffee to seafood places and the Walking Street night market within walking distance · So many people choose a light breakfast at the stay and then head out to try good food elsewhere for other meals · For food lovers this is a plus of staying in town, because you get to taste genuine Southern Thai food at prices the tourist-beach side can't match · If you're someone who values the experience of eating out more than a hotel buffet, this location is a fine playground

Service and guest care — Service is another point that earns consistent praise in real reviews of Lada Krabi Residence · Because it's a small, family-run stay, several staff get mentioned as friendly, helpful and happy to answer questions · Many reviews on both Trip.com and TripAdvisor use "friendly" and "helpful" repeatedly, especially around helping book boat tours, calling cars, and giving directions to Ao Nang or Koh Lanta · For people coming to Krabi for the first time and still confused about connecting boats and cars, having someone to tell you "which pier, which boat, how much" cuts a lot of the stress · To be straight about it, since this is a small place, when it's busy or short-staffed the response can be slower than at a big hotel with a large team, and English communication may take a bit of patience at times · But on the whole, the goodwill and genuine care for guests is a strength that brings people back to review it positively, and one reason the service score here sits at a good level

What real reviews say (the good and the bad) — Pulling together Trip.com (scored 8.1 from 43 reviews) and TripAdvisor (3.9 out of 5 from 244 reviews, #4 of 29 stays in Pak Nam), the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: a central-town location within walking distance of the Walking Street night market and the pier, great value compared with the beach side, rooms cleaner than expected, comfortable beds, friendly staff who help arrange tours, and breakfast included with vegetarian options · On the watch-out side: the thing mentioned most often is noise — the walls between rooms are fairly thin, and some nights you can hear the room next door or the street outside · Next is Wi-Fi that's weak in some rooms, strongest in the lobby; air-con in some rooms that vents heat out onto the balcony, making the balcony warm in the evening; pillows some people feel are too firm; and a building that's starting to show its age given the opening year · These gripes are common for budget stays, and most can be solved by choosing the right room and setting expectations to match the price, rather than being a dealbreaker that puts people off recommending it

"Great value for a central-town location, lovely staff who help with everything · The one downside is the walls are a bit thin — on a night when the room next door was talking loudly, you could hear it. Next time I'll ask for an upper floor or an inner corner instead."

Price comparison and value — Lada Krabi Residence's starting rate is around THB 900/night at regular pricing (about 28 US dollars), and can drop below that in low season or with promotions · A larger room like the Deluxe Quadruple that sleeps 4 climbs to around THB 1,400–1,800 depending on the season, which split among 4 people is very cheap · In high season (November–February) prices move up with demand, but it still sits among Krabi's lighter-priced stays · Compared with stays on the Ao Nang beach side, where starting rates are often double, Lada Krabi Residence feels great value within the budget group meant to be used as a base for trips · The difference you save on the room can go toward boat tours, diving, or several more seafood meals · But understand that you're paying for "location and cleanliness," not "a resort vibe or sea views" · If the goal of the trip is to be out all day and come back to sleep, the value here is clear · But if you want to spend most of your time at the stay's own pool or beach, the same money is better put toward a beachfront resort

Good to know before booking — A few things help make the stay smoother · One, since it's a small stay with no website of its own, the easiest way to book is through an OTA like Agoda, Booking.com or Trip.com — compare a few since prices can differ quite a bit at times · Two, if you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise, specify when booking that you want an upper floor, a corner room, or a room away from the road, because the walls between rooms are fairly thin · Three, if you need to work online, plan for Wi-Fi in the room possibly being weaker than the lobby, or bring a backup data SIM · Four, make use of the stay's tour-booking help, especially if it's your first time in Krabi, because it saves time and gets you a reasonable price · Five, in high season (Nov–Feb) rooms fill up fast, so book ahead and pick a free-cancellation option if your plans aren't set · Six, if you're there on a Walking Street night-market day (Fri–Sun), leave time to wander and eat, because it's just a walk away

The bottom line — From all the real reviews, Lada Krabi Residence is the best fit for budget travelers who want to use Krabi Town as a base for island trips, with cleanliness and a location within walking distance of everything · A starting rate of about THB 900/night, a location within walking distance of the Walking Street night market and Chao Fah Pier, breakfast included, and staff who help arrange island tours make it good enough value that a competitor at the same price in this area is hard to find · If you're after a resort vibe, sea views, a pool, or a flawless brand-new room, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a resort on the Ao Nang or Railay side instead · But for a hands-on trip where you want to keep your money for boat tours and seafood, while getting a clean place to sleep in the best location in town — Lada Krabi Residence answers that need at a genuinely accessible price, and that's why it has stayed near the top of the budget stays in Pak Nam for years

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Lada Krabi Residence, Krabi

faq.q: Where is Lada Krabi Residence in Krabi, and what's nearby?
faq.a: Lada Krabi Residence is at 90/71-72 Maharaj Road, in the Pak Nam area, in the center of Krabi Town · About a 3–5 minute walk to the Krabi Walking Street night market, and about 5–7 minutes to Chao Fah Pier, where boats leave for Poda Island, Chicken Island and the Separated Sea · The transport stop to Ao Nang is nearby · Ao Nang beach is about a 20–25 min drive, and Krabi Airport about 20 minutes

faq.q: What's the starting price at Lada Krabi Residence, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 900/night for the Superior Double Room at regular pricing · There's a Deluxe Double and Deluxe Twin with a balcony at around THB 1,100, and a Deluxe Quadruple that sleeps 4 at around THB 1,600 · The stay has no website of its own, so book through Agoda, Booking.com or Trip.com and compare prices first · Prices move up in high season (Nov–Feb)

faq.q: Who is Lada Krabi Residence best suited to?
faq.a: It's a great fit for budget travelers, couples, and small families who want to use Krabi Town as a base for island trips · Built around being out all day and coming back to sleep · Suited to people who value a central-town location and price more than sea views or a swimming pool · Not suited to those who want to stay by the beach or spend most of their time on the stay's facilities

faq.q: Does Lada Krabi Residence have breakfast and a swimming pool?
faq.a: It has breakfast included in the room rate, served downstairs as a set with menu choices, with both Thai and American-style options, and vegetarian options too · But there's no swimming pool, since it's a small budget stay · There's a small massage/spa service, a 24-hour front desk, and free Wi-Fi (strongest in the lobby)

faq.q: Is Lada Krabi Residence noisy, and which room should I ask for?
faq.a: Many reviews note that the walls between rooms are fairly thin, and on some nights you can hear the room next door or street noise · If you sleep light, we'd suggest asking for an upper floor, a corner room, or a room away from the road when booking or at check-in · Anyone very sensitive to noise should bring earplugs

faq.q: How do you get to the islands or Ao Nang from Lada Krabi Residence?
faq.a: Very convenient · It's about a 5–7 minute walk to Chao Fah Pier, where you can take a boat to Poda Island, Chicken Island, the Separated Sea or Railay · For Ao Nang there are minivans/songthaews from the nearby transport stop, about 20–25 minutes · You can book island tours right at the front desk — staff help arrange them at a reasonable price · It's also handy as a base for onward rides to Koh Lanta or Tap Khaek
